<reason>Side A won the framing fight that decided the debate. B's opening built its strongest material (vagueness, line-drawing, regulatory capture) on the assumption that an outside adjudicator must certify harm; A's [A2.1]-[A2.2] correctly relocated the motion to the platforms themselves, which are the actors named in the resolution and the parties holding A/B, holdout, and churn data. B adapted competently ("no clean trigger, only contested tradeoffs"), but that is largely an argument about how much to limit, and A anticipated it by noting the motion's own "when" concedes the hard cases and asks only about the clear ones. A also landed the sharpest unrepaired hit of the debate: paid boosts sell a third party's visibility without that party's knowledge or consent, so "disclosure to the purchaser is not disclosure to the person being demoted" — B's sponsored-search/priority-mail reply never addressed the non-consenting demoted user or the zero-sum nature of the queue. A's shared-parent-company point against "switching costs are near zero" also went unanswered, and sits awkwardly beside B's own claim that Match Group dominates. B's best moment was the detection symmetry ([B2.4]) and its honest, non-contradictory resolution at [B4.3]-[B4.4] that markets need direction, not precision; A's counter that blind exit is just priced-in churn was a fair reply. A's closing overstated B4.1 slightly as "no duty at all," and B's closing correction was legitimate, but A still ended with the cleaner decision rule: someone must be answerable for a harm only one party can see. A's opening was clipped for length, a real execution cost, but the case survived it.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Pressure Question forcing B to say whether a platform seeing its own harm data owes any change, and B's bullet-bite at [B4.1]. B's "every feature would be banned / tradeoffs are contested even with perfect data" was a coherent answer, but it left A with the clean crystallization that vagueness only argues about how much to limit, never that the answer is nothing — the strongest single exchange, closely followed by A's unanswered point that a boost sells a non-consenting third party's suppression.</best_rebuttal>
